Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: Idol manga, Idol manhwa. Use for: comics where the main theme of the story is about idols or celebrities, or the search to become an idol, sometimes linked to famous singers, entertainers or multimedia stars, such as stars of K-pop, as well as fictional idols or groups

Code.CodeDescription: Graphic novel / Stripboek / Manga: Moderne en hedendaagse fictie / literatuur
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: comic books that are works of fiction or original stories, that do not fall into another fiction genre. Use with: F* or YF* codes to give further details of fiction genres where required. Prefer: XQB for novels or other works of literature that were adapted into comics Zie ook: XQB

Code.CodeDescription: Graphic novel / stripboek / manga: actie en avontuur
Code.CodeNotes: Use with: FJ* or YF* codes to indicate genre as appropriate, for example for war stories use with FJM* codes, for martial arts stories, use with FJD, or with YFC* codes for comics aimed at children or teenagers

Code.CodeDescription: Graphic novel / stripboek / manga: horror / bovennatuurlijk
Code.CodeNotes: Use with: FK* or other F* or YFD codes to indicate specific genres, plus VXQ* or YNX* codes as appropriate

Also class here: comic books featuring sports, athletic and competitive pursuits. Use with: FG or YFR for works of fiction and S* or YNW* codes for non-fiction works to give more specific details of which sport as appropriate

Code.CodeDescription: Graphic novel / stripboek / manga: superhelden en superschurken
Code.CodeNotes: Use with: other XQ* codes as appropriate
Use with: FL* or YFG* codes to give further details of science fiction genres where required

Code.CodeDescription: Graphic novel / Comic book / Manga: Science fiction: Mecha and robots
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: Super-robots, real robots, transforming robots, armour, machines, AI technology

Code.CodeDescription: Graphic novel / stripboek / manga: fantasy, esoterisch
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: comic books featuring traditions of mythical, secret or esoteric knowledge, or particular fantasy genres. Use with: FM* or YFH*codes to give further details of fantasy genres where required, plus VXQ* or YNX* codes, as appropriate

Code.CodeDescription: Graphic novel / Comic book / Manga: Fantasy: Magical Girl / Magical Boy / Magical Creature
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: maho shojo, majokko. Use for: comics featuring characters with magical abilities

Code.CodeDescription: Graphic novel / Comic book / Manga: Fantasy: Portal fantasy / Isekai / Other worlds

Code.CodeDescription: Graphic novel / stripboek / manga: antropomorf / dierenverhalen
Code.CodeNotes: Use with: other XQ* codes as appropriate

Code.CodeDescription: Graphic novel / Stripboek / Manga: Traditionele verhalen, mythen, legendes
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: mythic fiction, retellings. Use for: stories that often have a long and continuous existence through multiple generations, stories that get told and retold, traditional local folktales, tall tales, folklore, folk literature, wisdom tales, cautionary stories, teaching stories, origin tales, or any form of traditional story told or retold, or modern retellings or works inspired by traditional stories, mythology, legends, fairy tales or folklore in comic book or any sequential art form. Use with: FN* or YFJ or YFH codes to indicate specific genres or QR* or YNRU codes for non-fiction works plus PLACE1* qualifiers, to indicate a particular tradition, as appropriate

Code.CodeDescription: Graphic novel / Comic book / Manga: Slice of life
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: Iyashikei. Use for: stories that are based on ordinary, everyday life, or parts of a character’s life, or a sequence of events in a characters life or mundane experiences in a characters life
Use with: FR* or YFM codes to give further details of romance genres where required

Code.CodeDescription: Graphic novel / stripboek / manga: school / studentenleven
Code.CodeNotes: Use with: other XQ* codes or F* or YF* codes to indicate genre plus 5L* code as appropriate
Use with: other XQ* codes as appropriate or WH* codes or YFQ as appropriate

Use with: F* codes for specific genres of historical fiction aimed at adults or YFT for historical fiction aimed at children or teenagers, OR with specific N* codes for adults or YNH* codes for works aimed at children or teenagers that are non-fiction history titles about particular periods or topics in history, and use with PLACE * plus TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers as appropriate

Code.CodeDescription: Graphic novel / Stripboek / Manga: Religieus, spiritueel, inspirerend
Code.CodeNotes: Use with: INTEREST 5PG* qualifiers, F* or YF* for specific genres of fiction, or QR*, VX* or YNR* codes for non-fiction titles

Use for: comic books designed for adults featuring scenes of an overtly adult nature or dealing with graphic themes only suitable for an aware, mature audience. Use with: Qualifier 5X plus other X* codes as appropriate Zie ook: XAMX

Use for: comic books designed for adults featuring scenes of an overtly erotic nature or dealing with graphic sexual themes only suitable for an aware mature audience. Use with: Qualifier 5X plus other X* codes as appropriate Zie ook: XAMX2

Code.CodeDescription: Graphic novel / stripboek: volwassenen - extreem geweld / bloederig
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: comic books designed for adults featuring scenes of an overtly violent or gory nature or dealing with graphic or disturbingly violent themes only suitable for an aware mature audience. Use with: Qualifier 5X plus other X* codes as appropriate Zie ook: XAMX

Code.CodeDescription: Graphic novel en stripboeken / manga: gidsen en recensies
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: History of Comics, comic studies. Use with: other subject codes as appropriate, for example, with FZ for Companion works or DSB* for histories of comic books or GB* codes for reference works, or DS* for works that analyse, study, critique comic books or Graphic narrative studies, AKLC* for works about comic book art or Sequential art studies, or other subject codes for titles about comics Zie ook: DSR FZ

Also class here: Strip cartoons, humorous comic strips or funnies. Use for: collections of typically humorous cartoons, usually originally published in newspapers or magazines or online Zie ook: YNUC

Use all Y* codes for: material aimed at, or purposefully written or created for a juvenile or adolescent audience (except for graphic novels, comic books, manga in X*). DO NOT USE: code ‘Y’ itself, but select specific categories from section Y*. Use all Y* codes with: only one INTEREST AGE 5A* Qualifier to indicate a guideline starting interest age (detailed age ranges should be included in other metadata) – or for YP* use EDUCATIONAL PURPOSE 4* qualifiers. All other qualifiers can be used as appropriate with Y* codes. DO NOT USE for: material intended primarily for adults that may also appeal to older teenagers. For ‘new adult’ content see note at 5LKE, for ‘Young Adult’ use the most appropriate 5A* Qualifier according to local usage of the term. NB: Y* codes should be used along with X* codes for graphic novels, comic books, manga. Y* codes may be used in combination with A*– W* codes but always prefer Y* codes and if mixing Y* codes with A*– W* codes, the Y* code must ALWAYS be designated as the Main Subject and sent with one 5A* qualifier. If sending A*– W* codes as Main Subject, then Y* codes should NOT be included except for JNU / JNUM with YP* or DSYC for reviews or critiques

Code.CodeDescription: Boeken voor zeer jonge kinderen, prentenboeken en activiteitenboeken
Code.CodeNotes: Use all YB* codes for: physical or digital items – the headings relate purely to the content, not the format (Format information is described in other metadata). Use all YB* codes with: only one INTEREST AGE 5A* Qualifier to indicate a guideline starting interest age

Use all YBC* codes for: highly illustrated books (typically colour throughout) for children in which the content (either fiction or non-fiction) is conveyed through the use of words and pictures in combination or through pictures alone. A ‘picture book’ differs from a ‘book with illustrations’, in that the pictures it contains are at least as important as the text (if any) and form an essential component of the book. Use all YBC* codes with: other codes from Y* sections as appropriate, for example, YNB for Picture book biographies, or YPCA21 for picture books that are part of a structured reading scheme

Use for: usually small format, board, bath, cloth or rag books, picture books with little or no text, and no explicitly educational early learning content, and usually very little story. Use with: YBG* codes for baby books which involve interactivity, or with YBL* codes if there is a significant theme or topic and with one 5AB* INTEREST AGE qualifier

Code.CodeDescription: Prentenboeken, boeken gebaseerd op bepaalde personages
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: all books based on TV or film characters, and all books featuring established pictorially-represented characters used in several books and or other products

Also class here: wordless or almost-wordless picture stories. Use for: fully illustrated storybooks for children where the narrative is told mostly or entirely through pictures and where any text is totally dependent on the illustrations. Use with: relevant YF* codes to indicate the genre of story, as appropriate, or YN* or YX* categories as secondary codes for stories with specific themes. YBCS should usually be the primary or main subject when used with YF*, YN* or YX* categories. Prefer: X* codes for stories told in comic book or manga form Zie ook: XA* XQ*

Use for: works that are collections or individual stories to be read out loud or listened to by children at bedtime or works about getting ready for bed, going to sleep and bedtime routines, preparing children for bedtime or works that are purposefully created to help soothe or calm a child down and prepare them for sleep or help them to sleep, or are stories about dreaming or dreams
Use for: picture books featuring use of imagination and/or play, for example with toys, often to create an imaginary world

Use for: children’s storybooks that are primarily text, but still contain plentiful illustrations. Usually of a relatively short length and low complexity, divided into very short chapters, and intended for transitioning readers – those moving on from picture storybooks. Use with: relevant YF* codes to indicate the genre of story, as appropriate, or YN* or YX* categories as secondary codes for stories with specific themes. Prefer: X* codes for stories told in comic book or manga form Zie ook: YBCS XA* XQ*

Code.CodeDescription: Interactieve en activiteitsboeken en pakketten voor kinderen
Code.CodeNotes: Use all YBG* codes for: children’s (of any age group) activity and interactive products; works where the primary purpose and main content of the product is an activity that requires participation and interaction, i.e. something to do or make, whether single use (e.g. press out and make, sticker books) or repeatable (e.g. touch and feel, making noises or sounds, etc). Use all YBG* codes with: other Y* codes as appropriate, and with 5H* qualifiers for activities linked to a specific holiday or season. Prefer: other Y* codes as the main category when the primary content (story or the subject) is more important than the interactivity. NB: Detailed format information is always described in other metadata

Code.CodeDescription: Interactieve en activiteitsboeken voor kinderen: tekenen, kleuren en schilderen
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: books to colour in, magic painting books, books and painting sets, fingerprinting, rubber stamps, connect the dots, dot to dot, paint-by-numbers, stencil books, doodles, finger painting, learning to draw or paint, books to draw in, etc Zie ook: YNA

Code.CodeDescription: Interactieve en activiteitsboeken voor kinderen: kijk-, ontdek- en zoekboeken
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: ‘magic eye’ or ‘3D’ books, optical illusions, wimmelbooks. Use for: material where aim is to look for and find item or character in pictures, or which have illustrations packed with details to find, but do not necessarily tell a story Zie ook: YNVP

Code.CodeDescription: Interactieve en activiteitsboeken voor kinderen: knutselen met papier
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: origami, books of paper dolls to dress, paper models to make or assemble, things to cut out or punch-out, dioramas, paper folding, or other activities for children using paper or card

Code.CodeDescription: Peuters en kleuters: ontwikkeling en leerconcepten
Code.CodeNotes: Use all YBL* codes for: pre-school material only. Use all YBL* codes with: other YN* or YX*codes to give extra detail of a significant theme or topic if appropriate and one 5AB* INTEREST AGE qualifier
Also class here: ABC and alphabet books, first word books etc

Code.CodeDescription: Vroege jaren: vers-, rijm- en woordspel
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: nursery rhymes and simple verse for very young children, tongue-twisters etc Zie ook: YDP YFV

Also class here: Pre-handwriting skills, pregraphism or pre-graphics skills and activities, writing readiness skills, activities for learning to hold a pen or pen or pencil control and skills, tracing exercises and activities, tracing different types of lines, patterns and shapes. Use for: works that help children acquire the fundamental skills children need to develop before they are able to write or draw
Also class here: telling the time, day and night, days of the week, seasons of the year, etc
Also class here: baby animals
Also class here: elements of daily life for very young children: bath time and washing, meals and eating, getting up, getting dressed, brushing teeth, looking after hair, etc

Also class here: titles that talk about poo, wee and farts. Use for: works that explain bodily functions linked to going to the toilet, as well as titles for teaching children how to use a potty or toilet

Code.CodeDescription: Vroege jaren: het lichaam en de zintuigen
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: sounds and noises, touch and feel, tastes and smells, fingers and toes, smiles and laughter, faces, peek-a-boo, hide-and-seek, etc
Use with: YXF* codes as appropriate
Also class here: books on ships, planes, trains, trucks, cars, bikes, buses, diggers, tractors, and other moving vehicles for the very young
Use all YD* codes with: INTEREST AGE 5A* Qualifiers as appropriate

Also class here: all annuals, yearly publications, periodicals or similar aimed at children or teenagers. Use for: material published every year, usually dated and thematic. Use with: second Y* code indicating type or subject area where possible
Use with: other code denoting literary form where appropriate, e.g. with a YF* code for fiction anthologies, with YDP for poetry anthologies. Use alone for anthologies of various literary forms
Zie ook: YBLB YFV

Code.CodeDescription: Kinderen / tieners: fictie en waargebeurde verhalen
Code.CodeNotes: Use all YF* codes with: one 5A* INTEREST AGE Qualifier; with PLACE 1*, TIME PERIOD 3* or INTEREST 5* Qualifiers where these aspects are particularly pertinent and significant; with appropriate non-fiction categories YN* or YX* to indicate key settings or topics of the narrative, but NOTE for ALL Children’s and teenage fiction the primary category MUST be an YF* code; with 5H*, 5J*, 5L* or 5P* qualifiers when these represent a significant topic or part of the appeal of the narrative; with 5X, where appropriate, to indicate material that may have themes or topics only be suitable for older or mature teenagers; with YB* to indicate the genre of a picture or chapter book; with YDC for fiction anthologies; YFZ* codes may be used to indicate special features of a fiction title. Prefer: X* codes for fiction told in comic book or manga form Zie ook: XA* XQ*
Use for: children’s and teenage fiction widely regarded or presented as ‘classic’ and typically but not necessarily published and in print for several decades

Use for: all contemporary non-genre fiction for children and teenagers. Use with: YX* or YN* codes to highlight the main theme of the story, for example, social issues, realistic or gritty fiction can be indicated using appropriate YX* codes, when the major theme is growing up or coming of age, use YXW, a story about illness use with YXL*, etc

Code.CodeDescription: Kinderen / tieners: fictie: actie- en avonturenverhalen

Code.CodeNotes: Use for: books, physical or digital, where the reader can select from options to alter the narrative outcome. Use with: other YF* code indicating genre Zie ook: YFZW

Code.CodeDescription: Kinderen / tieners: fictie: misdaad en mystery
Kinderen / tieners: fictie: leger en oorlog
Kinderen / tieners: fictie: horror- en spookverhalen, griezelverhalen
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: scary stories of the paranormal, gothic ghost stories, contemporary and realistic horror stories. Use for: any story that is written to be scary or to give an age appropriate feeling of fear, including stories that turn out not to be scary, stories that feature ghosts (friendly or scary), monsters (frightening or misunderstood), witches (wicked or misrepresented), creepy settings, characters or beings, haunted houses or is any form of supernatural chilling, spooky or scary story. Use with: YNX* codes for stories about specific supernatural or paranormal beings, such as YNXB3 for ghost stories, or other YF* codes, such as YFQ for funny or comedy ghost or horror stories, YFJM for cautionary tales, YFH* for fantasy scary stories, YFHG for horror stories based on myths, YFHT for Dark fantasy horror stories, YFA for classic ghost or horror stories, etc Zie ook: YNXW

Code.CodeDescription: Kinderen / tieners: fictie: speculatieve, dystopische en utopische fictie
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: fiction set in dystopian or utopian societies, alternative history fiction. Use with: YFG or other YF* codes if possible

Code.CodeDescription: Kinder- / tienerfictie: Apocalyptische en post-apocalyptische verhalen
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: end of the world stories, dying earth, collapsing or collapsed civilizations. Use for: stories set in worlds trying to prevent, or experiencing or that have already been affected by an apocalypse event, such as runaway climate change, an impact event, resource depletion, nuclear holocaust, pandemics, end times, zombie apocalypse, cybernetic revolts, technological singularity, invasion from space, dysgenics, etc
Use for: stories for children or teenagers with a superhero character or where the main characters are depicted as superheroes

Use with: YNTT for Time travel, time slip, or time loop sci-fi stories, YNXF for stories about extra-terrestrials or UFOs, YNNZ for stories about space travel, YNTC for stories about AI, Mecha, robots or new technology, etc

Also class here: Galactic empires, interstellar or intergalactic wars. Use for: science fiction stories set in space, in imagined galaxies or universes, or on different planets, often with advanced cultures and sophisticated technology and usually featuring main characters who are children or teenagers

Also class here: dieselpunk, cyberpunk, retrofuturism. Use for: science fiction based on an alternative world where, for example in the case of steampunk, 19th century steam power has emerged as the dominant technology

Also class here: paranormal fantasy, enchanted journeys, alternative worlds, accidental travel, portal fantasy, Isekai. Use all YFH* codes with: YNX* codes as appropriate, with YNXB* codes for stories featuring the paranormal or particular supernatural beings

Code.CodeDescription: Kinder- / Tienerfictie: Epische fantasie / heroïsche fantasie
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: sword and sorcery fantasy, quest fantasy, high fantasy

Code.CodeDescription: Kinderen / tieners: fictie: magisch realisme en fantasie
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: Magical girl. Use for: works that incorporates fantastic, magical, mythical or supernatural elements into an otherwise real-world or mundane setting, or works where the magic itself – whether a magical object or a character with magical powers – is the subject of the story, rather than simply a means to an end. Use with: YNXW for stories about witches, wizards or magicians or YNXB* codes for other magical creatures

Code.CodeDescription: Kinder- / Tienerfictie: Mythische fantasie / Mythische fictie
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: Myths or legends from any culture told or retold as fiction or in story form, mythological fiction, Arthurian fantasy, Classical fantasy (based on Greek and Roman myths), Shenmo (Gods and Demons), etc. Use for: fiction that is inspired by, or a retelling of, or that in some way draws from the characters, stories or themes of myth, legend, for example, a story based on a popular myth or character from a classic work in a modern setting or a story based on a minor character’s perspective, or that takes a ‘what if’ approach or create a mashup of different genres, for example, legendary character or hero meets dystopian future, or mythology crossed with contemporary adventure story. Use with: PLACE 1*, LANGUAGE 2*, INTEREST 5* Qualifiers to indicate if the story is taken from a particular tradition Zie ook: YNRU YFJ

Also class here: Medieval, Dark Age, Arabian, Celtic, Gunpowder, Prehistoric, Wuxia fantasy. Use for: fantasy that incorporates fantastic elements, such as magic or supernatural beings, into recognisable historic settings, periods, cultures etc. Use with: PLACE 1* and/or TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers to indicate setting as appropriate

Also class here: Romantasy, romantic fantasy, vampire romance, paranormal romance etc. Use for: Fantasy stories using many of the elements and conventions of romance but that is primarily a fantasy novel. Use with: YNXB* codes for romance stories featuring the paranormal, supernatural or particular supernatural beings, 5X code if content is more explicit and INTEREST AGE 5A* Qualifiers as appropriate
Use for: fantasy stories with darker and frightening themes, often incorporating elements of horror or that have a gloomy and threatening atmosphere or a sense of horror and dread
Use for: fantasy set in the present day or recognisably contemporary settings (according to the time period of its creator)

Also class here: Fables, stories that have a long and continuous existence through multiple generations, stories that get told and retold, stories from particular cultural traditions, stories written down from oral traditions, tall tales, myths or legends retold in a story form. Use all YFJ* codes for: modern retellings in story form or collections of these type of traditional stories aimed at children / teenagers. Use with: PLACE 1*, LANGUAGE 2*, INTEREST 5* Qualifiers as appropriate Zie ook: YFHG

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage fiction and stories: Folk and Fairy tales
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: Fairy tale retellings, fractured fairy tales. Use for: folk and fairy tales from any culture told in a story form, or retellings of these stories, stories inspired by fairy tales

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage fiction and stories: Trickster tales
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: stories that feature a trickster character such as a spirit, a deity, a human or an animal

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage fiction and stories: Creation, founding, origin stories
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: stories about the origins or beginnings of peoples, worlds, places, traditions, etc

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage fiction and stories: Teaching stories
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: Cautionary tales, Wisdom tales. Use for: stories that were created for the transmission of wisdom, knowledge, cultural traditions, oral transmission of stories, or stories that warn or caution young people about specific dangers, to teach a lesson or a general moral issue

Code.CodeDescription: Kinderen / tieners: fictie: religieuze / spirituele fictie
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: Faith-inspired or inspirational stories. Use for: fiction that promotes a particular religious, spiritual or visionary message or viewpoint. Use with: 5PG* values from INTEREST 5* Qualifiers or YNR* codes, to indicate the religious tradition, as appropriate

Code.CodeDescription: Kinderen / tieners: fictie: verhalen over relaties - romantiek, liefde of vriendschap
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: stories that deal with all kinds of relationships with others; for stories where interpersonal relationships are the main theme; or explore the relationship of the main characters, stories that explore relationships within groups, relationships between young people. Use with: YX* to give details of kinds of relationships as appropriate, for example, YXH for stories about relationships in peer groups or relationships with adults from a young persons perspective, 5PHG for stories about found or chosen family Zie ook: YXHB

Use for: instructional study material or activity books, meant to complement formal educational structures, usually designed for learning during the long holiday between educational years or grades, usually meant to revise topics already learnt and prepare for the transition to the next educational year or grade, and often presented in a fun, activity based format. Use with: EDUCATIONAL 4* qualifiers to indicate levels, plus use with other YP* codes for particular subjects or just YPZH if it covers all the main subjects covered in an academic year

Use for: material about problem solving using pictures and diagrams, or material aimed at improving the ability to understand and analyse visual information and solve problems, such as, identifying relationships, similarities and differences between shapes and patterns, recognizing visual sequences and relationships between objects, and remembering these

Use for: material about problem solving using words and letters, or material aimed at improving understanding, thinking or reasoning using concepts framed in words, or material that helps evaluate the ability to think constructively, rather than just simple fluency or vocabulary recognition
Use with: other Y* codes to indicate subject of reference material

Code.CodeDescription: Kinderen / tieners: naslagwerk: woordenboeken en talen
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: monolingual dictionaries for school or home use, other language reference works and titles about languages and language skills, word lists, vocabulary, grammar, usage guides, etc. Use all YRD* codes with: LANGUAGE 2* Qualifiers, as appropriate. Prefer: YPC* codes for materials for use in a formal educational structure Zie ook: YPC*

Code.CodeDescription: Kinderen / tieners: naslagwerk: tweetalige / meertalige woordenboeken
Kinderen / tieners: naslagwerk: studie van vreemde of tweede talen en referenties

Code.CodeDescription: Kinderen / tieners: naslagwerk: encyclopedieën, algemene naslagwerken
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: non-subject-specific works only; for subject-specific reference works, use YRG
Also class here: subject specific dictionaries / glossaries. Use with: another Y* code indicating the subject or scope of the reference work, YP* codes for material designed for education

Code.CodeDescription: Kinderen / tieners: naslagwerk: atlassen en kaarten
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: collections of maps for children, atlases that present different topics for children. Use with: other Y* codes as appropriate and with: PLACE 1* Qualifiers, as appropriate

Code.CodeDescription: Kinderen / tieners: persoonlijke en sociale onderwerpen
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: problems, issues, debates or challenges for youth or young people, situations and skills associated with these topics. Use all YX* codes: for titles dealing with any of these subjects either as non-fiction, factual approach or through stories or narratives. Use all YX* codes with: appropriate YF* code for fiction, stories or narratives where the main themes are personal or social topics, or with other Y* or XQ* codes to give greater detail for works dealing with these topics or issues through other subjects, with 5* INTEREST qualifiers when topics applies to particular interests. NB: YX may be used with J* or VF* codes to indicate there is no specific Y* code or qualifier but if mixing YX codes with J* or VF* codes, the YX code or another Y* code must be designated as the Main Subject and sent with a 5A* qualifier

Code.CodeDescription: Kinderen / tieners: persoonlijke en sociale onderwerpen: lichaam en gezondheid
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: advice for sleeping well, brushing teeth, dental and mouth hygiene, visiting the dentist, looking after the body, hygiene topics. Use for: popular health approaches to looking after the body, health and well-being. Use with: YXL* codes for mental health topics linked to the body and health

Code.CodeDescription: Kinderen / tieners: persoonlijke en sociale onderwerpen: fitness, lichaamsbeweging en gezond eten
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: personal health and hygiene, taking care of teeth, looking after your body, being active, food and health, nutrition and diet, topics around weight, veganism, vegetarianism, workouts and fitness routines for young people

Code.CodeDescription: Persoonlijke en sociale onderwerpen voor kinderen / tieners: yoga, meditatie, mindfulness
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: works about yoga or related practical techniques for mental and physical health and well-being for young people

Code.CodeDescription: Persoonlijke en sociale onderwerpen voor kinderen / tieners: Haar en haarverzorging
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: taking care of hair, brushing hair, titles about loving your hair, hair loss, alopecia, hairdos and hairstyles, etc

Code.CodeDescription: Kinderen / tieners: persoonlijke en sociale onderwerpen: seksuele opvoeding en levensfeiten
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: works that discuss or explain to young people aspects of sex and sexuality advice including, but not limited to, maturing, consent, sexual relationships, physical intimacy, sexual health, sexual attraction, sexuality and social media, sexual boundaries, talking about sex, contraception, birth control, dealing with sexual pressure, where do babies come from, pregnancy, etc

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage personal and social topics: puberty
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: works that explain puberty and the changes to the body, periods, menstruation, the menstrual cycle, changes to moods, hormonal changes, etc

Code.CodeDescription: Kinderen / tieners: persoonlijke en sociale onderwerpen: LGBTQ+
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: works that discuss or explain to young people aspects of LGBTQIA+ or queer life, culture, identities, history, events, health, wellbeing, sexuality, relationships, biographies, stories, dealing with prejudice, discrimination or any of the multiple aspects of LGBTQIA+ life. Use with: 5PSG, 5PSL, 5PT, 5PU, 5PV, 5PW or other 5* INTEREST Qualifiers as appropriate or YF* codes for stories that are about these topics, any YN* or other YX* codes for general interest or non-fiction works, for example, YXA* for works about health or body, YNH for LGBTQIA+ history, YNB for biographies, YXQ* for works about violence or abuse based on LGBTQIA+ identity, etc

Use for: works that tell stories of, examine or give advice to young people about LGBTQIA+ person‘s process of, or journey to, recognition, personal acceptance and disclosure to others of their sexual orientation or gender identity. Use with: other subject codes and 5P* INTEREST Qualifiers as appropriate

Code.CodeDescription: Kinderen / tieners: persoonlijke en sociale onderwerpen: genderidentiteit
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: titles that deal with anything to do with gender for young people, for example what it means to be a girl or boy or questions about identity. Use with: other codes as appropriate to give more information Zie ook: YNMF YNMH

Code.CodeDescription: Kinderen / tieners: persoonlijke en sociale onderwerpen: zelfbewustzijn en zelfbeeld
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: topics and advice about self-discovery, self-knowledge, self-worth, self-image, self-identity, self-reliance, building confidence

Code.CodeDescription: Kinderen / tieners: persoonlijke en sociale onderwerpen: emoties, humeur en gevoelens
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: general titles about emotions or titles that deal with multiple emotions. Use all YXE* codes for: titles that deal with several or various emotions, what they are, how to recognise them, how to deal with them, or understand them, express them, or encourage them

Code.CodeDescription: Emoties bij kinderen / tieners: woede, frustratie
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: coping with anger, disgust, hostility, jealousy, selfishness, feeling grumpy, tantrums, bad temper or mood, rage

Code.CodeDescription: Emoties bij kinderen / tieners: verdriet, ongeluk, teleurstelling
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: gloominess, emotional pain or suffering

Code.CodeDescription: Emoties bij kinderen / tieners: zorgen, angst
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: feeling worried or anxious, dealing with worries, distress, uncertainty, stress, fear, separation anxiety, shame, embarrassment

Code.CodeDescription: Emoties bij kinderen / tieners: eenzaamheid, isolatie
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: feeling like an outsider or a loner, feeling alone or lonely, feeling alienated

Code.CodeDescription: Emoties bij kinderen / tienerss: mededogen, empathie, vriendelijkheid
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: accepting differences, solidarity with or compassion for others, courtesy, generosity, tolerance, love and understanding

Code.CodeDescription: Emoties bij kinderen / tieners: moed, dapperheid, hoop
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: heroism, perseverance, persistence, loyalty, trust, honesty

Code.CodeDescription: Emoties bij kinderen / tieners: geluk, vreugde
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: pleasure, cheerfulness, contentment, gladness, delight, excitement, optimism, gratitude, thankfulness, optimism, mirth, elation, or just being happy

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage emotions: Mischief and mischievous behaviour
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: Being naughty, misbehaving, prankish, teasing, getting into trouble. Use for: works about causing or showing a fondness for causing trouble in a playful way, works that show the consequences of misbehaviour, or works where being naughty is a key theme

Code.CodeDescription: Kinderen / tieners: persoonlijke en sociale onderwerpen: families en familieleden
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: aunts, uncles, cousins, family life, multigenerational families, kinship groups, relatives, blended families, extended family members, stepfamilies or any type of family etc. Use for: works about families, issues in families, particular members of a family, etc. Use with: 5PHA* qualifiers

Code.CodeDescription: Persoonlijke en sociale onderwerpen voor kinderen / tieners: ouders
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: mothers, fathers, single-parents, step-parents

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage personal and social topics: Grandparents
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: Grandmothers, grandfathers, grandparents and their grandchildren

Code.CodeDescription: Kinderen / tieners: persoonlijke en sociale onderwerpen: echtscheiding
Kinderen / tieners: persoonlijke en sociale onderwerpen: adoptie / pleegzorg
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: orphans

Code.CodeDescription: Kinderen / tieners: persoonlijke en sociale onderwerpen: broers en zussen
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: brothers, sisters, step and half brothers and sisters

Code.CodeDescription: Kinderen / tieners: persoonlijke en sociale onderwerpen: nieuwe baby
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: new brother, new sister, new sibling, or titles about babies

Code.CodeDescription: Kinderen / tieners: persoonlijke en sociale onderwerpen: dood, overlijden en rouw
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: loss, dying, bereavement, mourning, works explaining death, how and why people die, end of life, etc

Code.CodeDescription: Kinderen / tieners: persoonlijke en sociale onderwerpen: zelfmoord
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: getting help or dealing with suicidal ideation or thoughts, helping understand when someone commits suicide, suicide prevention, advice for talking about suicide. Use with: 5JB for material specifically created for or aimed at young men or boys, 5JA for material specifically created for or aimed at young women or girls, 5PS*, 5PT for works aimed at LGBTQIA+ youth, or other 5P* qualifiers for works relating to specific groups, or 5L* for works about specific age groups, for example, 5LFE for works about older teenagers, 5PHA* codes when discussing family members, etc

Code.CodeDescription: Kinderen / tieners: persoonlijke en sociale onderwerpen: relaties (geen familie / groupen)
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: relationships within peer or social groups, interpersonal relationships, frenemies, cliques, gangs, learning about relationships, skills for interaction with others outside families and other relationship topics, relationships with adults from a young persons perspective, dealing with the adult world, etc

Code.CodeDescription: Kinderen / tieners: persoonlijke en sociale onderwerpen: vrienden en vriendschappen
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: making new friends, friendship groups, found family, issues around relationships with friends, such as conformity, popularity or isolation within a group of friends, end of friendships, advice about making friends, etc Zie ook: YFM

Code.CodeDescription: Kinderen / tieners: persoonlijke en sociale onderwerpen: daten, relaties, romantiek, en liefde
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: topics like first attraction, being in a couple, advice about romantic relationships, dating for the first time, first love, unrequited love, also advice about boundaries, consent and intimacy in a romantic relationship, kissing, advice for breaking up, ending a relationship, problems in relationships

Code.CodeDescription: Kinderen / tieners: persoonlijke en sociale onderwerpen: levensvaardigheden en keuzes
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: manners, behaviour, dilemmas, consequences, responsibilities, skills for interacting with modern life, other people, following or not following rules, getting into trouble, taking responsibility for actions, assuming the consequences, not using violence, not hitting, kicking or biting, etc

Code.CodeDescription: Kinderen / tieners: persoonlijke en sociale onderwerpen: tienerzwangerschap
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: teenage parenthood, teenage mums and dads. Use for: works aimed at young people explaining pregnancy, birth, parenthood or topics around being a young mother or father

Code.CodeDescription: Kinderen / tieners: persoonlijke en sociale onderwerpen: drugs en verslaving
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: topics around substance addiction, alcohol abuse, etc

Code.CodeDescription: Kinderen / tieners: persoonlijke en sociale onderwerpen: handicap en leerachterstand
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: physical disabilities and impairments, visible or invisible disabilities or conditions, wheelchair users, etc. Use with: 5PM* Qualifiers as appropriate

Code.CodeDescription: Kinderen / tieners: persoonlijke en sociale onderwerpen: fysieke en mentale gezondheidsproblemen
Code.CodeNotes: Use all YXL* codes for: titles aimed either at young people who have a particular condition or to help understand others who have a particular condition. Use all YXL* codes with: 5PM* Qualifiers as appropriate. NB: YXL* codes may be used with V* codes when there is no specific Y* code or qualifier but if mixing YXL* codes with V* codes, the YXL* code or another Y* code must be designated as the Main Subject and sent with a 5A* qualifier

Code.CodeDescription: Kinderen / tieners: persoonlijke en sociale onderwerpen: ziekte en specifieke fysieke gezondheidsproblemen
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: living with disease and long-term physical conditions, injuries, first aid, medicine, titles that explain specific illnesses, diseases, etc to young people. Use with: YNH for history of medicine, plagues and disease in the past, histories of pandemics and epidemics, etc

Code.CodeDescription: Kinderen / tieners: persoonlijke en sociale onderwerpen: kanker
Kinderen / tieners: persoonlijke en sociale onderwerpen: mentale gezondheid
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: mental disorders, trauma and traumatic experiences. Use for: works that help children or teenagers deal with mental health, personal trauma or traumatic events around them, how to process or talk about trauma, with adverse childhood experiences, advice about good mental health and wellbeing

Code.CodeDescription: Kinderen / tieners: persoonlijke en sociale onderwerpen: eetstoornissen en zelfbeeld
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: ARFID, anorexia, bulimia, binge eating, body dysmorphia, purging disorder, disordered eating, advice about body acceptance, body positivity, body neutrality

Code.CodeDescription: Kinderen / tieners: persoonlijke en sociale onderwerpen: angst, depressie en zelfverwonding
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: panic attacks, severe stress

Code.CodeDescription: Kinderen / tieners: persoonlijke en sociale onderwerpen: positieve / goede mentale gezondheid
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: positive self-image, well-being. Use for: works that explain, help or give advice about good mental health and wellness, about judging life positively and feeling good, positive wellbeing, positive images

Code.CodeDescription: Kinderen / tieners: persoonlijke en sociale onderwerpen: multicultureel
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: works on social and cultural topics linked to multiculturalism, pluriculturalism, biculturalism and multicultural, pluricultural or bicultural societies

Code.CodeDescription: Kinderen / tieners: persoonlijke en sociale onderwerpen: racisme en anti-racisme
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: xenophobia, race relations. Use for: works about discrimination and prejudice based on skin colour, race or ethnic origin, or prejudices based on the perception that someone is foreign or from outside the community, and issues of inequality and discrimination, as well as measures to address racism. Use with: YNH for historical topics Zie ook: JBFA1

Code.CodeDescription: Kinderen / tieners: persoonlijke en sociale onderwerpen: diversiteit, gelijkwaardigheid en inclusie
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: books that deal with these topics and stories with a particularly diverse cast of characters, or which illustrate accessibility, social justice, equity, diversity, or inclusivity (DEI) within the context of the story without necessarily being the subject of the story. Use with: YF* codes for stories and values from 5P* INTEREST Qualifiers as appropriate

Code.CodeDescription: Kinderen / tieners: persoonlijke en sociale onderwerpen: vooroordelen en intolerantie
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: discrimination, injustice, the judgements of others. Use with: YNH for historical topics

Code.CodeDescription: Kinderen / tieners: persoonlijke en sociale onderwerpen: pesten, geweld, misbruik en groepsdruk
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: use of violent or abusive language. Use for: works that explore these topics, often titles aimed at explaining or helping young people understand or deal with these topics. Use with: YF* when it is the major element of the story

Code.CodeDescription: Kinderen / tieners: persoonlijke en sociale onderwerpen: mishandeling
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: physical, mental, emotional or sexual abuse, coercive control, domestic abuse, or works aimed at young people about criminal exploitation, debt bondage, exploitation of vulnerable children by criminal gangs

Code.CodeDescription: Kinderen / tieners: persoonlijke en sociale onderwerpen: pesterij en intimidatie
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: online trolling and bullying, coercion, cyberbullying, cyberstalking, physical or verbal bullying or harassment, relational bullying, collective bullying or mobbing, bullies and accomplices, victims of bullying, effects of bullying and harassment, bystander effect, school bullying, victimisation

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage personal and social topics: Violence
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: Knife violence, gun violence, bombs, violent acts, acts of terrorism, kidnapping, violent threats, violent rampages. Use for: works aimed at young people dealing with physical violence or conflict involving weapons, helping young people deal with knife crime, with gun violence, stabbings, shootings, violent gang crimes, school shootings, violence of war, for works helping young people avoid violence, or deal with the trauma of weapons related violence

Code.CodeDescription: Kinderen / tieners, persoonlijke en sociale onderwerpen: persoonlijke veiligheid
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: dealing with strangers, road safety, safety in the home etc. Use with: YXZE for titles about personal safety in the event of an emergency

Code.CodeDescription: Kinderen / tieners: persoonlijke en sociale onderwerpen: weglopen
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: fugitives, escapees. Use for: works that look at young people that run away and reasons around this, running away from home, or family or school or escaping things like repression, slavery, conflict, etc. Use with: YF* codes for stories about runaways, with YNB for biographies of runaways, or YNH for historical approaches Zie ook: YXZM

Code.CodeDescription: Kinderen/ tieners: persoonlijke en sociale onderwerpen: school, onderwijs en docenten
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: works that explore topics like starting school, attending school, going to a new school, school life, education topics, titles about teachers and educators, school librarians

Code.CodeDescription: Persoonlijke en sociale onderwerpen voor kinderen / tieners: spijbelen en schoolproblemen
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: works about issues at school, around repeated absence, non-attendance, avoiding school, etc

Code.CodeDescription: Tieners: persoonlijke en sociale onderwerpen: advies over carrière en verdere opleiding, schoolverlaten
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: titles about work, jobs, careers, professions aimed at a young audience but not educational Zie ook: YPJV2 YPWC9

Code.CodeDescription: Kinderen / tieners: persoonlijke en sociale onderwerpen: eerste ervaringen en opgroeien
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: Dealing with and understanding change, talking about change, changes or new experiences like moving home, living in a new town, starting a new school, making new friends, a new family, new siblings, etc. Use for: titles that explore or deal with major or significant new experiences or change in the life or world of a young person, how to deal or cope with this experience or change, or explains about these experiences or changes, from the perspective of the child or teenager etc. Use with: other Y* codes or qualifiers to give more details of the main theme or experience

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage personal and social topics: Growing up / coming of age
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: titles that deal with the changes from childhood or youth to adulthood, such as taking on adult responsibilities, career choices, character growth, gaining independence, self-reliance, moving away from home, going to university, first experience of love, etc. Use with: YF* for coming of age fiction, YXA* codes for works about changes to the body, or sex, YXHL for first love, etc

Also class here: social activism, general works on social justice. Use for: titles that deal directly with the topics or explain debates around social issues for young people. Use with: other YX* codes to give greater detail; YF* fiction codes for stories that are about these topics. NB: YXZ may be used with JBF* codes if there are no more precise Y* codes but if mixing YXZ with JBF* codes, a Y* code MUST be designated as the Main Subject and sent with a 5A* qualifier

Code.CodeDescription: Sociale onderwerpen voor kinderen / tieners: activisme / activisten
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: titles about social activism, environmental activism, human rights, social or civil rights movements, causes and other forms of engagement as activists by young people, volunteering or volunteer engagement. Use with: other YN* or YX* codes to give greater detail and with YNB for biographies of activists

Code.CodeDescription: Sociale onderwerpen voor kinderen / tieners: identiteit / erbij horen
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: titles that explore topics or themes around notions of identity and belonging, as individuals or as part of a particular group or communities, identity or belonging based on relationship to a place, based on a shared culture or heritage or other works that explore the notion of identity or belonging for children or teenagers

Code.CodeDescription: Sociale onderwerpen voor kinderen / tieners: vrede / verzoening
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: works for young people about peace after conflict, maintaining peace, ideas for creating, keeping, spreading peace and peaceful actions, resolving conflict, themes and topics around reconciliation between different groups or persons

Code.CodeDescription: Sociale onderwerpen voor kinderen / tieners: ongevallen, rampen of noodsituaties
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: either works about the impact or consequences, on both people and society, of both natural and human-made disasters and accidents; things such as diseases, plagues, epidemics, pandemics, famine, malnutrition, volcanic explosions, earthquakes, extreme-weather, floods, forced movement of peoples as a result of disasters; or works about accidents like fires, crashes, shipwrecks, maritime and air disasters or accidents, rail or road accidents, explosions, oil spills, getting trapped or lost, etc; or for titles that explain how to prepare for disasters, emergencies, etc for example, what to do during an earthquake, or major fire or tsunami

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage social topics: Fame, celebrity, fandom
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: works for young people about fame, celebrity, being famous, the search for fame and the issues with being famous or a celebrity, being an idol, being glamorous or wealthy, or works about being a fan or fandom

Code.CodeDescription: Kinderen / tieners: sociale onderwerpen: milieu en duurzaamheid
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: looking after our planet, climate change, pollution, rubbish, plastics, recycling, climate emergency, climate strikes, environmental champions, looking after our future, protecting nature, conservation, water use and conservation, managing natural resources, sustainable solutions, reducing consumption and use of resources. Use for: works that look at these topics and also ones that have ideas for solutions, or what young people can do themselves

Code.CodeDescription: Sociale onderwerpen voor kinderen / tieners: Armoede / paecariteit
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: works that look at social issues topics in society around social instability, deprivation and hardship, homelessness, the unhoused, hunger, economically disadvantaged, food poverty, etc

Code.CodeDescription: Kinderen / tieners: sociale onderwerpen: migratie en vluchtelingen
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: asylum seekers, immigrants and immigration, emigrants and emigration, displacement, exile, forced journeys or relocation, diasporas. Use with: YNH for history titles or YNB for biographies, YF* for stories and INTEREST 5P* qualifiers as appropriate

Code.CodeDescription: Kinderen / tieners: sociale onderwerpen: religieuze kwesties
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: titles that look at discussions, debates, topics, controversies, or other issues related to religion, belief, faith, religious identity, etc. Use with: YNR* or other Y* codes and 5PG* INTEREST qualifiers as appropriate

Use INTEREST 5* Qualifier codes WITH appropriate subject codes for: indicating a variety of characteristics relating to the main content of the particular work. 5A* age codes to qualify Y* codes, 5H* to indicate content about a particular holiday or event, 5L* to indicate content about a particular age group / generation, 5P* to indicate content about a particular grouping of people, etc. National extensions (i.e. 5*-xx- format codes, where ‘xx’ indicates a country code) can be assigned by any user, and are not exclusive to users in the indicated country. All 5* codes must be used to describe a main content or topic of the work. DO NOT USE: as a marketing target audience code, the 5* Qualifier must relate to the main content of a work. DO NOT USE: code “5” itself, but select appropriate specific qualifiers from section 5*

Use all 5A* age codes for: defining the Y* or X* codes – 5A* age numbers are used instead of named codes, such as juvenile, middle grade, young adult, as these have different meanings in different countries or languages. Select one 5A* code indicating a general guideline starting or base interest age of the content in any works aimed primarily at children or teenagers. All Y* codes (except YP* which use 4* codes) MUST be accompanied by one 5A* qualifier code to give guidance of interest age, for example: book content for an audience of 9 to 12 age group, should use 5AK, as the lower age; content of interest to teenagers should use 5AP or 5AQ; content for older teenagers and young adults should use 5AS, 5AT or 5AU as appropriate. 5AR, 5AX and 5AZ can be used with any relevant subject code. All 5A* codes can be used with X* subject codes if the Comic book is aimed at children or teenagers. DO NOT USE: 5A itself – always use 5A* codes. NB: Greater detail of age range, reading age, interest age etc would be communicated in other metadata

Also class here: High-low readers, Hi-Lo content aimed at children or teenagers. Use for: books that are specially written for or considered suitable for young people who do not want to read, have difficulty reading, or are struggling to read. Usually these books will have a higher interest age and a lower reading age. Content is usually aimed at a particular interest age but the language used is purposefully slightly simpler than most average content aimed at the same interest age in that language, so that it is easier to read or listen to than other titles. These are often titles in specific named collections and will often have notions of levels of difficulty associated with them by the publisher and / or may be accompanied by indications of complexity. Use with: one other 5A* Interest age qualifier. Prefer: 5AX for reluctant adult readers or 5AZ for accessible content and 4L codes for second language titles Zie ook: 5AX 5AZ 4L*

Code.CodeNotes: Use for: works aimed specifically at older teens and young adults in their 20s, those who are newly adult, emerging adulthood. This age group may be referred to in some places as young adults or sometimes as new adults. The content is specifically created for and about this group but can also appeal to other groups as well. Prefer: 5LKE for titles about this age group. DO NOT USE: with Y* codes Zie ook: 5LKE

Also class here: High-low readers, Hi-Lo content aimed at adults. Use for: books that are specifically aimed at adult literacy or helping adult readers with reading difficulties or books that are suitable for adult readers who are not confident in their reading abilities or suitable for the newly literate. Content is aimed at adult interests but the language used is purposefully slightly simpler than most average content aimed at adults so that it is easier to read or listen to than other titles
